pages.title: Rational Field
pages.text: Every fraction of one integer by another, which is enough to divide by anything except zero. Between any two rationals there is another, so the field is dense everywhere, yet the square root of two is nowhere in it. It shimmers like a fine mesh that hides countless holes.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I needed division, so I let a Casimir plate split the integer ring into finer and finer slices, mimicking how the vacuum between plates is divided into modes. Every ratio appeared, and with them, the unsettling gaps between them.
